Equipment:Earth Resistance Testing

Introduction
The GEOHM 40 D is a compact device to measure:

The 
earth resistance in electrical systems.

The soil 
resistivity which is important when dimensioning earthing systems.

The 
ohmic resistance of solid and liquid conductors.

Installing the battery.

Screw-tighten the bottom of the case.

After setting up the measuring circuitry as described above, perform the 
 measurement as follows:

sections.text:
There are two methods for 
measurements: Three wire method, Four wire method
Three Wire Method

Place the spikes for 
search electrode and auxiliary earth electrode at a distance of at least 20m and 
/ or 40 from the earth electrode (see figure 2).

Make sure there are no 
excessive transient resistance between search electrode and soil.

The earth electrode is 
connected to terminal "E/C1" of the tester with one test lead, the search 
electrode to terminal "S/P2". and the auxiliary earth electrode to terminal 
"H/C2".

Press the 3-pol 
pushbutton, and keep the pushbutton pressed at least until the diplayed value 
has stabilized (approx 10s)

Read the digitally shown 
measured value as well as the assigned unit in Ω or 
kΩ.

Check whether the above described display function 
cause signalling of faults.

Eliminate the signaled fault and restart the 
measurement.

When the pushbutton 3-pol is released, it is 
automatically disconnected.

The resistance of the test lead to the earth 
electrode is directly entered into the measured result.

To keep the error caused by the test lead as small 
as possible, for this method use a short connection lead with a large cross 
section between earth electrode and terminal "E/C1).
